segments.t: Every item in korTTY's menu bar, with its shortcut (where defined) and what it does. The menu bar can be hidden with KTPH003KTPH000KTPH004+KTPH005KTPH001KTPH006+KTPH007KTPH002KTPH008 and shown again by right-clicking the terminal or status bar.
Open Quick Connect in a new terminal tab
Open Quick Connect; the tab it opens is an KTPH000incognito sessionKTPH001 whatever the connection says. Greyed out when your organization forbids incognito sessions

Give the active terminal tab a name of its own instead of the connection's name or the KTPH000title its shell setKTPH001; an empty name shows that again. Available while a terminal tab is active. See KTPH002Working with tabsKTPH003

Close every other tab of the current window; the active tab stays open. Asks once when some of the closing terminals have split panes or a running command. The same entry is in a terminal tab's right-click menu. See KTPH000Working with tabsKTPH001
Close the tabs after the active tab, which stays open. Asks like Close Other Tabs. The same entry is in a terminal tab's right-click menu
Close every tab in the current window; Reopen Closed Tab brings the terminal tabs back

Reopen the terminal tab you closed last (or the tabs one command closed together) with a new session; greyed out while there is nothing to reopen. The same entry is in a terminal tab's right-click menu. See KTPH000Working with tabsKTPH001

What you closed, newest first, also before korTTY last quit: a tab, the tabs one command closed together, or KTPH000Window: …KTPH001 for the tabs of a closed window. Choose an entry to reopen it; KTPH002Clear ListKTPH003 empties the list
Open an additional, independent main window

Restore a saved project: its first window replaces the tabs of this window, each further window opens in a new window, and every window gets its position, size, tabs and active tab back. See KTPH000WindowsKTPH001

Under KTPH001ConnectionsKTPH002, the saved connections you used last (up to 10, newest first, as at the top of Quick Connect), each opening a tab that signs in like KTPH003ConnectKTPH004 in the Connection Manager; under KTPH005ProjectsKTPH006, the projects you opened or saved last (up to 10), followed by the other projects in KTPH000, each opening like KTPH007Open Project…KTPH008. Files that no longer exist are left out. KTPH009Clear ListKTPH010 empties the menu without deleting a connection or a project file. See KTPH011Open RecentKTPH012
Save every open window with its position, size and tabs as a project (KTPH000)

Reopen the windows and tabs korTTY had open before this start, which it saves on its own while it runs: the first window opens in this window when it has no tabs, otherwise in a new window, and every further window in a new window; tabs that need a password, a new temporary SSH key or the locked vault wait in the restore bar. Greyed out while there is no previous session and after you restored it once. See KTPH000Previous sessionKTPH001
Create an encrypted backup (ZIP password or GPG)
Connection entries (Quick Connect, Manage/Import/Export Connections) live in the KTPH000ConnectionsKTPH001 menu.

Search the active tab (terminal scrollback or open editor). On Windows and Linux a focused terminal sends KTPH002KTPH000KTPH003+KTPH004KTPH001KTPH005 to the shell, so open Find from this menu or the terminal's right-click menu there

Label every web address, path, e-mail address, UUID, IP address, git hash and number of four or more digits in the focused terminal pane, and every match of KTPH001your own patternsKTPH002; type a label to copy its text, or KTPH003KTPH000KTPH004 and the label to open a web or e-mail address, or in SSH and local-shell tabs a file path in the Snippet Editor. Disabled outside terminal tabs, see KTPH005Quick selectKTPH006

Scroll the focused terminal pane to the prompt before the one you are at, using the marks of a shell set up for KTPH000shell integrationKTPH001; when it cannot, the status bar says why. Disabled outside terminal tabs
Scroll the focused terminal pane to the next prompt its shell marked, or back to the bottom after the last one. Disabled outside terminal tabs

Select what the last finished command printed in the focused terminal pane, using the marks of a shell set up for KTPH000shell integrationKTPH001; the status bar says what was selected, or why nothing was. Disabled outside terminal tabs
Copy what the last finished command printed in the focused terminal pane to the clipboard, without changing the selection. Disabled outside terminal tabs
Connect to a host without saving
Open the Connection Manager (tree, search, edit)
Open the dual-panel SFTP file manager
Open the SFTP file manager on the focused terminal pane's own SSH session, in the folder its shell is in
Enter the master password to unlock stored secrets when the startup prompt is off (disabled while unlocked)
Manage stored credentials (encrypted). The shortcut also works while a terminal has the focus
Manage GPG keys used for backup encryption
Review, search and remove trusted SSH host keys
Open the global Settings dialog (all tabs)

On macOS and Windows, enable activity-based system-sleep prevention. The computer is kept awake only while a terminal is connected, an enabled Scheduler job has a future run or is running, or an AI request is in progress. With none of these activities, system sleep remains available even while the item is checked. Display sleep is unaffected. On Linux the item is visible but disabled.
See the KTPH000Settings referenceKTPH001 for every individual setting.
Create, edit, organize, send and export command snippets in one workspace: the library and the snippets you edit as tabs, each with its stored Full code analysis
Schedule background command / snippet / AI-agent / AI-swarm / SFTP / Rsync jobs
Manage terminal recordings and export to WebM/MKV via KTPH000
Toggle recording of the active terminal (KTPH003KTPH000KTPH004+KTPH005KTPH001KTPH006+KTPH007KTPH002KTPH008)
Manage KTPH003session journalsKTPH004: search, open, rename, describe, export and delete them, and set the journal options (KTPH005KTPH000KTPH006+KTPH007KTPH001KTPH008+KTPH009KTPH002KTPH010)
Toggle the session journal of the active terminal tab; starting mid-session imports the existing scrollback (KTPH003KTPH000KTPH004+KTPH005KTPH001KTPH006+KTPH007KTPH002KTPH008)
Snapshot the active terminal into its running session journal (KTPH003KTPH000KTPH004+KTPH005KTPH001KTPH006+KTPH007KTPH002KTPH008)
Two tabs in one dialog: KTPH000Text BannerKTPH001 renders text as a FIGlet banner in multiple font styles, KTPH002AI PictureKTPH003 lets an AI profile draw a subject as ASCII art
The three session-journal items stay visible but are disabled when an KTPH000enterprise policyKTPH001 denies the session-journal feature.
Manage AI profiles, integrated GGUF models, RAG knowledge stores, the AI Skills library, and Text/Coding roles
Open the saved AI chat conversations directly in their own window; invoking it again brings the existing window to the front
Broadcast one AI task to many servers and compare the answers (KTPH003KTPH000KTPH004+KTPH005KTPH001KTPH006+KTPH007KTPH002KTPH008)

KTPH000AI ManagerKTPH001 opens as a modeless window, so it can remain visible while you use the main window. Invoking it again restores and focuses the same manager for that main window instead of creating a duplicate. Its five sections are KTPH002ProfilesKTPH003 (connection mode, model, prompt preset, reasoning, internet access and token budget), KTPH004Local ModelsKTPH005 (search/download/import GGUF models), KTPH006Knowledge StoresKTPH007 (RAG sources), KTPH008AI SkillsKTPH009 (the skill library, moved here from the global settings dialog) and KTPH010Local AIKTPH011 (Text/Coding/embedding roles and the local runtime). The open primary section remains marked by a bold accent underline after you move focus into its tables, fields, or buttons:

Open the KTPH000command paletteKTPH001 to find and run any menu command or a terminal command such as KTPH002Clear BufferKTPH003, switch to an open tab, connect to a saved connection or run a snippet in the terminal, by typing part of its name; the shortcut also works while a terminal has the focus and with the menu bar hidden, and closes the palette again

Open the command palette with KTPH000 already typed, so it lists only the KTPH001snippetsKTPH002 and runs the one you choose in the focused pane of the terminal; a shortcut you assign also works while a terminal has the focus, and closes the palette again
Dock the local KTPH000file browserKTPH001 to the left of the terminal; unchecking the active side hides it
Dock the local KTPH000file browserKTPH001 to the right of the terminal; unchecking the active side hides it

Slider (0–100 %) that makes the terminal background see-through to the desktop while the text stays sharp; every split pane inherits the value. The value is saved across restarts; fullscreen temporarily renders terminal backgrounds opaque and restores the value when you leave. Switching it on or off needs a restart, so the status bar shows a hint when you cross that threshold. Shown in the in-window menu bar only.

Split the focused pane of the active terminal tab on that pane's own server, as KTPH003Split Right (same server)KTPH004 or KTPH005Split Down (same server)KTPH006 in its right-click menu does: the new pane goes to the right when the pane is wide and below it when it is tall, and gets the keyboard focus (see KTPH007Split operationsKTPH008). On macOS the key is KTPH009KTPH000KTPH010+KTPH011KTPH001KTPH012+KTPH013KTPH002KTPH014
Split the focused pane on that pane's own server, with the new pane always to the right / below
Close the focused pane of the active tab without asking; the keyboard moves to the first remaining pane. Disabled while the tab has a single pane
Panes ▸ Focus Pane Left / Right / Above / Below

Move the keyboard focus to the KTPH002split paneKTPH003 on that side of the focused pane in the active tab; at the edge of the tab nothing happens. Available while the active tab has two or more panes. On macOS the keys are KTPH004KTPH000KTPH005+KTPH006KTPH001KTPH007 with an arrow key
Move the keyboard focus to the next or previous pane of the active tab, starting over after the last one

Let the focused pane of the active tab fill the whole tab, or show all its panes again; the check mark shows whether a pane is zoomed. Splitting, closing or moving a pane and moving the focus to another pane show all panes again as well (see KTPH003Split operationsKTPH004). Available while the active tab has two or more panes. On macOS the key is KTPH005KTPH000KTPH006+KTPH007KTPH001KTPH008+KTPH009KTPH002KTPH010
Panes ▸ Broadcast to All Panes of This Tab

Switch the active tab's KTPH000broadcast modeKTPH001 on or off, as KTPH002Extras → Broadcast ModeKTPH003 in a pane's right-click menu does; the check mark shows whether it is on. Switching it on needs two or more panes

Let the focused pane of the active terminal tab take part in KTPH000multi-execKTPH001, so what you type in it also goes to the other panes that take part, in any tab and window, or take it out again; the check mark shows whether it takes part. KTPH002Extras → Multi-exec: Include This PaneKTPH003 in a pane's right-click menu does the same for that pane
Multi-exec ▸ Include All Panes of This Tab
Let every pane of the active terminal tab take part in multi-exec, or take them all out when they all take part; the check mark shows whether they do. The tab's right-click menu has the same entry
Multi-exec ▸ Include All Terminals of This Window
Let every pane of every terminal tab of this window take part in multi-exec
Take every pane of every window out of multi-exec, as KTPH000StopKTPH001 in the status bar does. Available while a pane takes part
Switch KTPH000keyword highlightingKTPH001 on or off for the focused pane of the active tab; switching it back on restores the set the pane showed last. Applies to the running session only

Choose the rule set the focused pane shows: KTPH000NoneKTPH001, a built-in set (KTPH002Errors and warningsKTPH003, KTPH004Network addressesKTPH005, KTPH006Network devicesKTPH007) or one of your own. Applies to the running session only
Open the KTPH000rule-set editorKTPH001 to create, change, duplicate or delete your own rule sets and look at the built-in ones; it opens on the set the focused pane shows
Show the whole korTTY window — menus, tabs and status bar included — kept at its previous window size and centered on an empty fullscreen background, hiding the desktop and other windows
Also hide scrollbars while in fullscreen
AI Agent Panel ▸ At Bottom / Dock Left / Dock Right
Choose where the AI agent activity panel lives
Live Journal ▸ Dock Left / Dock Right
Dock the KTPH000live journal panelKTPH001 beside the terminal; selecting the active side hides it
Toggle the live journal panel on its last-used side (right by default)
Coding Agents ▸ Dock Left / Dock Right
Dock the KTPH000Coding Agents panelKTPH001 beside the terminal; selecting the active side hides it
Toggle the Coding Agents panel on its last-used side (right by default)
Bring the next coding agent that is waiting for a decision to the front, across windows
Remote Files Sidebar ▸ Dock Left / Dock Right
Dock the KTPH000remote files sidebarKTPH001 beside the panes of every terminal tab; unchecking the active side hides it. Offered while the active tab has an SSH pane or the sidebar is on
Remote Files Sidebar ▸ Show/Hide Remote Files Sidebar
Show the remote files sidebar on the right, or hide it; hiding asks first while sidebar transfers are running
Configure shared connection sources and synchronization

The manual has its own text-size buttons at the top left of its window: KTPH000, the current percentage, and KTPH001. Clicking the percentage resets it. The same three actions have keyboard shortcuts: KTPH008KTPH002KTPH009+KTPH010KTPH003KTPH011, KTPH012KTPH004KTPH013+KTPH014KTPH005KTPH015, KTPH016KTPH006KTPH017+KTPH018KTPH007KTPH019. korTTY remembers the size, and the size covers the whole window — the page and, when it is open, the AI search panel beside it. See KTPH020Manual text sizeKTPH021.

Screenshots and diagrams enlarge on click: the picture opens over the page at the largest size the window allows, with KTPH002−KTPH003 / KTPH004+KTPH005 buttons and a percentage that returns it to that fitted size. Zoom further to read a single setting row, drag the picture to pan, and close with the KTPH006×KTPH007, KTPH008KTPH000KTPH009 or a click next to the picture. KTPH010KTPH001KTPH011 and the wheel zoom as well. The same works in the online guide.

On macOS the packaged app keeps running in the background (so the JobScheduler can run scheduled jobs) even after the last window is closed. korTTY therefore adds two extra entry points so it stays reachable — and quittable — with no window open:

KTPH000Dock icon menuKTPH001 — right-click korTTY's Dock icon for quick actions: KTPH002New WindowKTPH003, KTPH004New TabKTPH005, KTPH006Manage Connections…KTPH007, KTPH008Open Project…KTPH009, KTPH010ManualKTPH011, KTPH012About korTTYKTPH013, and KTPH014QuitKTPH015.
KTPH000Menu-bar (status) iconKTPH001 — a system-tray icon with KTPH002New WindowKTPH003 and KTPH004QuitKTPH005; clicking the icon opens a new window.
Both provide a reliable KTPH000QuitKTPH001 even when every window is closed.

The menu bar at the top of the screen stays as well when you close the last window, and while no korTTY window has the focus it can still be the menu bar of a window you closed. Its entries then act in the korTTY window you used last, which comes to the front, or open a new window first when none is open: KTPH000New TabKTPH001 opens Quick Connect there, KTPH002Manage Connections...KTPH003 the Connection Manager. KTPH004New WindowKTPH005, KTPH006QuitKTPH007, KTPH008Prevent System SleepKTPH009, KTPH010Stop Multi-execKTPH011 and cancelling a running job need no window. KTPH012Close TabKTPH013, KTPH014Close All TabsKTPH015, KTPH016Close WindowKTPH017, KTPH018Close PaneKTPH019, KTPH020CutKTPH021, KTPH022CopyKTPH023, KTPH024PasteKTPH025, KTPH026Broadcast to All Panes of This TabKTPH027 and the three KTPH028IncludeKTPH029 entries of KTPH030View → Multi-execKTPH031 do nothing from the menu bar of a closed window, so they never close a tab or a pane, paste into it or change where your typing goes in a window you are not looking at.
